content.comment_body: Hello! I have several empty network connections that are blocking my Ethernet ports. How can I remove these? My network setup involves one parent [product_name] communicating with three child devices and one [version_no] compatible device. This setup requires most Ethernet connections available on the parent [product_name]. When I copy and paste a [document] diagram between the child devices, the network connections update (they turn red and swap to IP instead of device mode), resulting in both new and leftover connections. Over time, these unused connections accumulate and block ports. How do I clear them out when nothing is actually being exchanged?

This issue typically occurs when you copy and paste parts of your program that have network components initially created via drag and drop. It's a frequently discussed problem on forums. To avoid it, I personally refrain from using drag & drop. In network project mode, you can't delete these unused connections. However, if you export individual diagrams, modify them externally, and then rebuild your network project, you may be able to remove them. Please share your project file for further review.

Thank you [user_name] for your explanation! I agree, copy and paste can be problematic, especially with entire diagrams. I found a straightforward solution: First, manually fix as much as possible and confirm that broken connections are truly unused. Close [product_name] software. Unzip the project file (it's just a zip archive). Open the .xml file inside—it defines your network project setup. In the devices section, look for entries representing manual connections and remove them. Re-zip the project files, restart [product_name], and you'll find the blocked ports are available again. This code section is what I successfully deleted.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face issues with persistent empty network connections after copying and pasting diagrams in their network projects, which leads to blocked Ethernet ports. The software does not permit straightforward deletion of outdated connections, so users resort to manual edits of project files. This points to challenges with the software's network management features, particularly in terms of user-friendliness and reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to remove unused or obsolete network connections directly within the software's project interface, rather than through manual file editing. They also anticipate that copy and paste actions will be handled more reliably, preserving network connections accurately without creating extra or inaccessible ports.
